title: Frederica Wilson marks Indigenous Peoples' Day, honors Ben Crump, and celebrates Miami Heat - North Miami-Dade News
text:
U.S. Representative Frederica Wilson, who represents Florida’s 24th district in Congress, published a series of tweets on October 13 and 14, 2025, covering topics from Indigenous Peoples’ Day to sports and birthday wishes to a prominent attorney.
On October 13, 2025, Wilson wrote, “Today on #IndigenousPeoplesDay, we honor the rich histories, cultures, and resilience of Indigenous communities. Let’s celebrate and support the incredible contributions of Indigenous communities today and every day.”
The following day, October 14, 2025, she posted, “Happy birthday to my friend, a fearless champion for justice, America’s Black Attorney General, Ben Crump!”
Later that same day, Wilson tweeted congratulations to the Miami Heat and their coach, stating, “Congratulations to our @MiamiHEAT and Coach Spo! From Miami to the world, we’re proud to see #HeatNation leading @usabasketball at the 2027 FIBA Men’s World Cup and the 2028 Olympics! “
Frederica Wilson has served in the U.S. Congress since 2011, succeeding Kendrick Meek as the representative for Florida’s 24th district. She previously held seats in the Florida Senate from 2002 to 2010 and in the Florida House of Representatives from 1998 to 2002. Born in Miami in 1942, Wilson currently resides in Miami Gardens. She is a graduate of Fisk University, where she earned her BA in 1963.
